title: What the cheapest steps keep and make
claim: For bases of betweenness knots grown one distinction at a time with every old state kept: a single knot leaves N + d or 2N - d states (at least N + 2, reached only by subdivisions and pendants); the one-knot fewest-states rule keeps k and lambda (line (1,1), 2 x 2 (2,2), star (1,2)); one step from a line makes at most two orders and keeps a line only at the n + 1 placements; the zero-cost three-knot steps of a line are exactly the C(n,3) fills, each two orders (from one knot: the 2 x 2 cut system, unique); from one knot fewest states with three knots gives the 2 x 2 at n = 4 and 8 options at n = 5. S6 (cubes at n = 2^d) is a conjecture.
standard_statement: Split systems of betweenness bases; chromatic number of the split-incompatibility graph and lattice dimension (chain covers of nested oriented splits) under single-distinction extensions.
prior_work: Buneman 1971; Bandelt and Dress 1992; Bandelt and van de Vel 1989; Eppstein 2005; Klavzar and Mulder; KNOT-ORDER-20261117-001; GRID-GROW-20261117-001.
